resolved_findings: Original saturation rates suggested a simple curve without matching one Michaelis–Menten model. Final 5.0, 8.0, 9.4 are the one-decimal values of 10*S/(1+S) at S=1,4,16.
'For the same invented reaction' implied continuity with a profile having a different delta G. Final 'For an invented reaction' removes that referent.
checks: Energy profile 1: delta G=-12, forward barrier=48, reverse barrier=60 kJ/mol. Catalyzed profile: delta G=-8, forward barrier=24, reduction=18, reverse barrier=32 kJ/mol.
Maintained saturation and unchanged turnover justify doubling active enzyme giving 20 micromol/L/s. Qualitative saturation does not claim an inferred mechanism or measured biology.
The simple reversible competitive model supports increasing substrate reducing fractional inhibition. Separate-site regulation is not mislabeled as a complete kinetic inhibition class.
Feedback answer concerns relief of reversible inhibition at the first enzyme, without asserting immediate whole-pathway maximum flux.
All 12 designated answers remain uniquely supported under their stated assumptions; other options conflict with those assumptions.
